change.summary: Acknowledge a manual next-request route only after the private atomic routing-state write succeeds, while serializing route selection/mutation and rechecking the semantic-stream boundary.

test_first.command: timeout 30s node --test --test-name-pattern='does not acknowledge a manual preference' packages/account-router/test/runtime-persistence.test.mjs

before_implementation.observed_failure: A fixture route store that rejected every save still received HTTP 200 accepted instead of a sanitized 503.
before_implementation.bounded_cleanup: The runtime cleanup absorbed the expected stop failure and the command exited normally in 90 milliseconds.

additional_failure_injections: manual acknowledgement remains pending while the private save is blocked
manual persistence failure returns sanitized 503 without publishing a switch
a semantic stream starting during candidate persistence rolls the candidate back and returns 409

covers: HTTP/SSE bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
WebSocket bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
durable manual acknowledgement and semantic-race rollback

deployment.reason: The previously proven sudo root-GID transition failure and non-writable /opt/codex-account-router boundary are unchanged.

remaining_limits: 0.2.12 is verified but is not active until a host-privileged operator runs the rollback-capable router-only deployment script.
The short route-mutation critical section covers local scheduling, credential acquisition and private state writes; no production latency claim is made before deployment measurement.
A private routing-state persistence failure makes manual switching and later selection fail closed until an operator resolves the state boundary.
The test uses synthetic accounts only and does not qualify a real A-to-B switch.
Real two-account verification remains blocked until explicit enrollment authorization.
